mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate level (FEDFUNDS) indicates tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns is greater than or equal to 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above its 50th percentile.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment rate above 5.0% (UNRATE) signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Combined high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%) and rising policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%) signal aggressive monetary tightening to combat inflation, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 5.0% and FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, declining housing starts (HOUST < 1100) combined with slowing GDP growth (GDPC1 < 1.5% annualized) signals weakening demand that reduces corporate revenue expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion, when HOUST < 1100 and GDPC1 < 1.5%, 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the joint condition over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 100,000 jobs/month) signals a robust labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000, 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0) signals manufacturing contraction and supply chain disruptions that reduce corporate output and profits, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 100.0, 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST < 1100) and industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0) signals dual demand-supply contraction that reduces economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1100 and INDPRO < 100.0, 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the joint condition over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%), rising inflation expectations increase market uncertainty and discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%), 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.
